clue.text: Peter's occupation provided backing to general

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the word for provided from back to front

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'
William Sherman was a US Civil War general

explanation.surface: Someone asks what Peter did for a living, and it involved supporting a general.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is Saint Peter the apostle, who fished on the Sea of Galilee before following Jesus; 'backing' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter worked with nets on Galilee before becoming an apostle, so his trade was catching fish.

clue.text: Refuse to be gripped by impassioned rabble-rouser

indicators.note: to be gripped by means held inside, so this word goes into the next

parts.note: fired, as in fired up, means impassioned
bran is the husks left over from milling grain, treated as waste

explanation.surface: Garbage is clutched by a passionate agitator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' wants to be the verb (to decline); it is the noun, waste, here husk.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand stirs up trouble or revolt, like an agitator who rouses a mob.

clue.text: Capital! In Chesterfield I .

indicators.note: In tells us the letter goes inside the word for the furniture

parts.note: a Chesterfield is a deep-buttoned leather sofa
taken as written

explanation.surface: A line that seems to start a sentence about the English town of Chesterfield, running into 3 down.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterfield is a town in Derbyshire, England, but here it is the leather sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: …can get in trouble doing an impersonation

indicators.note: in trouble means in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing 2 down: someone in Chesterfield gets into a scrape by mimicking someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges CANGETIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor playing a part is impersonating a character, which is what acting means.

clue.text: Government department responsible for car's tax

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car, so car's gives Mini's
to tax someone is to try their patience

explanation.surface: A government office is in charge of motor taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax' looks like duty, but it is the verb meaning strain; 'responsible for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministries are the departments of state headed by ministers, such as defence or health.

clue.text: Almost starting — not before time

indicators.note: starting points to the first letter of the word after the dash

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Nearly getting going, but not ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean very close to but not quite, as in 'almost done'.

clue.text: Prancing about by …

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
per means by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: An unfinished line about someone prancing, running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 9 across, but each clue works on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip and frolic, and a caper is a playful leap, so it stands for prancing.

clue.text: Good hunters did, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is the sound of another

parts.note: hunters chased their quarry

explanation.surface: Fine hunters did well, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and virtuous, abstaining from sex, a sense of morally good.

clue.text: Cleric eats beef next

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: a primate is a senior archbishop
beef comes from the ox

explanation.surface: A churchman tucks into some beef next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' as an animal is the ox.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest or immediately adjacent, as in a proximate cause.

clue.text: Rewriting both her and my lines…

indicators.note: rewriting means the letters are set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: Redrafting verses about two people, running into 14 down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rewriting' rearranges HER and MY; 'both' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme is a short verse, a few lines of poetry.

clue.text: …chorus has to stop

explanation.surface: Continuing 6 across: the dancing goes on until the chorus line must halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A song's repeated section is its burden, and to hold back from doing something means to stop.

clue.text: Little woman curbs a rise of desire

indicators.note: curbs means holds in, so the woman's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: A small woman keeps a growing passion in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' is not about size: Amy is one of the four sisters of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory describes things relating to love or sexual longing, so it fits an adjectival phrase meaning concerning desire.

clue.text: Snake starts to slither towards crow

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A snake begins slithering in the direction of a crow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' looks like the bird the snake is after, but it is the verb meaning brag.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag loudly about one's success, which is what boasting means.

clue.text: A singleton diamond in card game

explanation.surface: A lone diamond appears in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem set alone in a ring has this name, and it is also patience, the card game for one player.

clue.text: Social workers revise man's role

indicators.note: revise means change, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Social workers are asked to rethink a man's role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revise' rearranges the letters of MANSROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Almoners were hospital social workers in Britain, originally people who distributed alms.

clue.text: … in badly directed film anything may ensue

indicators.note: may ensue means comes after, so this piece follows the one for film

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, such as a mist on glass
aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: Continuing 8 down: a poorly directed movie where anything could happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but is a thin coating; the leading 'in' only links from 8 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mistaught is to be wrongly instructed, given bad direction.

clue.text: Turns rock round

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for rock is written backwards

parts.note: to rock is to sway from side to side

explanation.surface: Something spins a stone around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns SWAY back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or aircraft yaws when it swings off course about its vertical axis, so it turns.

clue.text: Incidental information is turned up with glee

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read upwards, so the little word is reversed

parts.note: glee means delight

explanation.surface: Side information is taken up with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses IS to SI; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a piece of incidental information shedding light on a subject.

clue.text: Some motley paper

explanation.surface: A piece of multicoloured paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A jester's costume was motley, and a fool's cap was part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester's belled hat was part of his motley outfit, and the name passed to a large paper size.

clue.text: Peculiar observation made about city

indicators.note: made about means wrapped around, so one word holds the other

parts.note: espial is the act of spying, observation
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: An odd remark was passed about a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' looks like strange, but it means particular.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means special or particular to one person or thing.

clue.text: Some said I should finish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Somebody remarks that they ought to wrap things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to dish someone's chances is to ruin them, bringing them to an end.

clue.text: Drops the cracked and broken piece of china

indicators.note: cracked means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drops the cracked china and it shatters into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges DROPSTHE; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a shard of broken pottery, which archaeologists dig up.

clue.text: Thin coating of blue applied to hotel

indicators.note: coating means covering all round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: the sky is the blue
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A thin layer of blue paint is put on a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' wants to be a noun describing paint, but it is the verb: the blue wraps the hotel; 'of' and 'applied to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means very thin, lean or slender.

clue.text: The Talisman' produced by a scholar, a man from Abbotsford

parts.note: an MA is a master of arts, a scholar
Abbotsford, in the Scottish Borders, was Sir Walter Scott's home

explanation.surface: Scott's novel The Talisman, written by a scholar at Abbotsford.
explanation.walkthrough: The Talisman is a Scott novel, so the surface is about him; but a talisman is a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky charm, an object believed to bring good luck.

clue.text: Exclude the last pot

explanation.surface: Keeping someone out, or sinking the final ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, a game played on a table with coloured balls, the black is usually the last ball potted.
explanation.definitionFit: To vote someone out of a club is to blackball them, and in snooker the black is the final ball sunk.

clue.text: Outspoken dame

explanation.surface: A frank-speaking lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad humour is frank and coarse, and in American slang a broad is a woman, like dame.

clue.text: Stand while slippery character is about

indicators.note: is about means goes around, so the eel's letters surround the other word

parts.note: an eel is slippery, and the phrase also describes an untrustworthy person
as means while, as in 'as I was leaving'

explanation.surface: Standing by while a slippery fellow hangs around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery character' sounds like a crook, but it is the eel.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame on legs that holds a painting or blackboard, an artist's stand.

clue.text: One having confessed about going to court

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the letter

parts.note: to sing is slang for confess to police
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who confessed is heading to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having confessed' is criminal slang: someone who has sung to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Suing is taking legal action, going to law against someone.

clue.text: No cigar can be made without using chemicals

indicators.note: can be made suggests the letters are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: A cigar cannot be produced without chemical processing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made' rearranges NOCIGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic farming avoids artificial fertilisers and pesticides, so its produce is grown chemical-free.

clue.text: Noisily closing up part of room

indicators.note: noisily says we want a word that sounds like another, heard rather than read

parts.note: sealing means closing up, as with an envelope

explanation.surface: Loudly shutting part of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceiling is the overhead surface of a room, opposite the floor.

clue.text: Spotted bats

explanation.surface: Someone spotted some bats.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern covered in small marks is dotted all over, and someone a bit crazy is described as bats.

clue.text: Superior fellow is brought in to a difficult situation

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: is brought in means the abbreviation goes inside the next word

parts.note: a plight is a difficult or dangerous situation

explanation.surface: A top man is brought in to sort out a tricky situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is brought in' places the fellow's letter after the P of the difficult situation, which follows 'to' as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest rank or class, the best available.
